canonical_claim: Before the cache-over-CA fix, a `<type>cache</type>` disk over CA failed closed at `IDisk::startup` with code 48 `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` because the generic cache metadata wrapper hid the CA write path. Additionally, A cache disk over a content-addressed disk originally failed at startup because MetadataStorageFromCacheObjectStorage did not forward isContentAddressed or the content-addressed transaction surface. Additionally, For a content-addressed disk, `DiskObjectStorage::wrapWithCache` reuses the CA metadata storage and wraps only the object storage with `CachedObjectStorage`. Additionally, Under cache-over-CA, immutable content-hash blobs are read through `CachedObjectStorage`, while refs, manifests, GC, and writes use the CA metadata storage's raw uncached object-storage pointer. Additionally, The cache-over-content-addressed fix reuses the content-addressed metadata storage directly and wraps only the object storage layer.

Writable startup rejects configurations where `attempt_timeout + lease_safety_margin >= mount_lease_ttl`, and effective timeout-controller values are exposed in logs.; The initial configuration invariant is `attempt_timeout + lease_safety_margin < mount lease TTL`; the current 30-second attempt timeout with a 30-second lease TTL is rejected for protocol-significant writer operations.
The decommission-to-heal flow is two-phase: the first call refuses with rows in `Removing`, a GC round deletes the catalog-only rows, and the second call retires the slot.

A stateless/ref-less reader that attaches by reading the catalog and registers no `/parts` ref is invisible to the per-process `use_count()==1` MARK-union fence, which is a valid cross-node fence only for replicas holding a `/parts` ref; owning replicas can release refs after `old_parts_lifetime` (480s) mid-SELECT, sweeping the manifest/blobs out from under the read. The preferred fix is an ephemeral reader pin (a Keeper node or equivalent) created at query start naming the parts/snapshot read, auto-released on session end/crash; this is distinct from the lost-replica timeout, which is a genuine leak needing a separate long-dead-replica reaping rule.
`PartFolderView::fileSize` reports mutable value length, inline byte length, or blob size according to the matching file representation; `inlineBytes` returns bytes only for inline entries.
Global jemalloc profiling is enabled with `<jemalloc_enable_global_profiler>1</jemalloc_enable_global_profiler>` in server XML and requires a server restart; sampling begins at boot.
On the Atomic layout, `moving` already occupies the parser's part-directory position, so the L1 fix adds a `route()` case rather than changing `findPartDirComponent` for that layout.

The normative `getView` algorithm first resolves the ref, returns `nullptr` for absence without retaining it, validates a retained view for `CachedForLoad`, builds through `readManifestShared` on a miss, retains only eligible non-strict results, and then returns the view.; With caching enabled, `getView` checks an active slot and shared map, resolves the ref, reads and validates the `PartManifest`, builds the view, and publishes it only if local cache state still matches.

The T15 trace dump SELECT aliased `'${tt}' AS trace_type`, and ClickHouse alias resolution in `WHERE` caused the literal to shadow the table column, so the dump was an unfiltered mix of trace types until fix `52f110e94b3`.

A regular GC round acquires a lease, computes a heartbeat floor, folds shard journals into attempt artifacts, performs only previously published `delete_pending` deletes, publishes retired-list runs, and advances all state with one `gc/state` CAS.

The orphan-manifest sweep can delete a committed manifest when a hot LIST omits the logs that grant its owner, because activeManifestKeys trusts only the incomplete reconstructed set; Orphan cleanup protects current owners and every manifest removed in the unadopted tail using the exact adopted `RefBaseSet` plus the complete validated writer tail. Additionally, An orphan-manifest sweep uses the newest snapshot plus every later log, including manifests removed in the tail, and additionally requires the durable `last_folded_ref_id` before deleting a retired manifest. Additionally, The orphan-sweep protection view combines the newest snapshot with the complete tail, protects owners and manifests removed anywhere in the tail, retains the young-manifest window, and requires the `last_folded_ref_id` condition.; The orphan-manifest sweep proves build retirement, reads the exact adopted `RefBaseSet`, replays the complete contiguous tail, rechecks `gc/state`, and deletes only candidates absent from the complete protection set.; The orphan-manifest sweep protects every current committed or precommit manifest and every removed manifest named by exact chain nodes above the GC cursor, and deletes only a listed eligible manifest with its exact current token.

The persisted in-degree authority is the set of active source edges identified by `(ManifestId, path)`, with edge IDs computed by `sourceEdgeId(ManifestId, path)`; `in_degree(blob)` is the cardinality of that active source-edge set during a round and is not persisted as a separate counter.; CAS blob in-degree is a SET of source edges with last-wins semantics per key, not a counter; an unmatched removal is a per-key no-op and cannot remove a sibling manifest edge for the same blob. Additionally, The in-degree reducer models source edges as a set: an unmatched `-1` is dropped as a no-op and a duplicate `+1` collapses, so the reducer must not materialize negative edges merely to repair the retention leak. Additionally, The unmatched removal-fold `-1` is harmless under the current edge-set model because source edges are set membership keyed by `(ref, ManifestId, path)`, not a counter; erasing an already-absent edge cannot affect another manifest's edges. Additionally, In-degree is a set-presence merge keyed by `(blob, source_id)` and applied in strict transaction-id order; a `del` whose key is absent is a silent no-op. Additionally, The source-edge reducer treats in-degree as a set: an unmatched `-1` must be dropped rather than materialized as a negative edge, because a negative edge could cause a false deletion.

`encodePartManifest` returns canonical uncompressed text for text-size budgeting; backend PUTs seal that text, backend GETs open it before decoding, and exchange remains text-to-text without wrapping.

The first statement of the ref walk's `while (expected)` loop is `if (*grounding->committed_through < *expected)`, and `grounding` is not reassigned while `expected` re-enters through that ceiling, so every later body statement runs with `*expected <= *grounding->committed_through`. Additionally, Ref-walk termination relies on `_ckpt.committed_through` being a round-start snapshot read once per namespace; the remaining proof-producing exits are `resolved_through == *grounding->committed_through` and `nextRefLogIdWithinCommittedFrontier` returning `nullopt` after an applied record. Additionally, A record arriving after a round's LIST is either at or below `committed_through`, where the walk folds it, or above it, where the walk stops at the ceiling with `resolved_through == *committed_through`; neither case leaves the namespace unproven. Additionally, Inside the ref-walk loop, `grounding` is non-null and the first ceiling test compares `expected` with `*grounding->committed_through`; after the ceiling and crossing paths, the loop body always satisfies `*expected <= *grounding->committed_through`. Additionally, The ref-walk frontier is finite because `committed_through` is a round-start snapshot, and a namespace cannot enter the walk with an empty `grounding` or empty `grounding->committed_through` optional.; The historical T6a deficit was caused by records appended above the old frozen tail; commit `357cf7b963f` introduced `_ckpt.committed_through` as the walk ceiling and proves the frontier at that ceiling instead of abandoning it.

The `admits()` rewrite uses exact framing-size helpers plus the running body counters rather than hand-written delta arithmetic, while preserving the existing `admits` signature and boolean decisions.

A GC round takes or renews the leader lease, collects source edges, folds per-shard in-degrees, condemns new zero-in-degree blobs, exact-token-deletes previously condemned blobs whose state is unchanged, and seals the round with one CAS on `gc/state`.

A GC rebuild reconstructs cursors and edges but reclaims nothing; blobs not named by a surviving manifest are retained as `unaccounted`.; `Gc::rebuildBaseline` writes only the GC plane—runs, seals, and `gc/state`—and never modifies ref shards, manifests, or blobs or deletes content. Additionally, `SYSTEM CAS GC REBUILD` writes only the GC plane, namely `gc/state` and `gc/gen/*` artifacts, and does not touch ref shards, manifests, or blobs or delete anything during the rebuild itself.
A ready parent cannot proceed to normal fold, `REBUILD`, `DEFER`, or a fresh-cut continuation while an eligible catalog deletion remains unresolved.
A removed namespace whose only residue is `_files` promotes its cleanup item to `Completed` on the first fold, so the janitor cannot key its reclaim logic off `Pending` state alone.
A referenced-but-missing or corrupt GC run, retired list, or adopted fold seal raises `CORRUPTED_DATA` and refuses the GC round until an operator performs GC rebuild.

`checkTableCanBeRenamed` must be forwarded by `StorageTableProxy`, not generic `StorageProxy`, because forwarding it generically would materialize a `StorageTableFunctionProxy` during metadata-only rename.

Forced REBUILD can discard a durable classification-4 hold and later certify the broken namespace as quiet, allowing a visible B:-1 to delete a blob still named by A:C+2.; With healthy authoritative `gc/state`, REBUILD carries all holds verbatim; with missing or undecodable `gc/state`, REBUILD has authority to reconstruct only, performs zero catalog deletions, and returns.

`_snap` remains under `stream/` because it is immutable and transaction-addressed, grouped with logs for recovery hints and covered-object cleanup; moving it to `state/` would require a second hot LIST or a simultaneous recovery-and-cleanup redesign. Additionally, `_snap` remains under `stream/` because it is immutable and sequence-addressed, is grouped with logs for recovery hints and covered-object cleanup, and avoids a second hot LIST; the stream/state split is by access pattern, not ownership.

GCS generation mismatches return HTTP 412 with the literal XML body code `PreconditionFailed`, so the existing ClickHouse detectors `finalizeConditionalWrite` and `removeObjectIfTokenMatches` require no change.
`Interpreters/SystemLog.h` registers the `ContentAddressedGarbageCollectionLog` and `ContentAddressedLog` system logs.
Part B issues no object-store request and cannot make a fence live; only the unchanged self-remount or late renewal path can make `mayMutate()` true.

The object-storage interface provides `removeObjectIfTokenMatches` for token-exact deletion and `copyObjectConditional` for write-once server-side copy with `If-None-Match: *`, both with fail-closed defaults.

Remote-confirm recovery needs its own budget because an LRU cache of `ref_table_cache_bytes` at 256 MiB can turn cycling confirmations across namespaces into a self-sustaining recovery storm; over-budget refusal is soft `Unknown` and must have a dedicated counter.

For trimmed-but-live precommits whose create event was trimmed, the rebuild lists `cas/manifests/` and over-protects manifests that are not committed, not named by a live-precommit binding, and not provably build-dead by `prefixEligible`.
`ContentAddressedMetadataStorage` remains responsible for path parsing, `PartRefKey` construction, freshness selection, and translation into `IMetadataStorage` return types.
Concurrency tests for A1, A3, and A7 must avoid `sleep` and use deterministic fault injection, instrumented backends, or an atomic-gated second thread.

A sweep-only defense that makes `activeManifestKeys` judge precommits dead was deferred because it would delete the manifest body without releasing the precommit's pinned blob edges; the fold-side fix is required.

Capture-at-deposition (recording `NamespaceLifeId` at fold time rather than re-deriving it from the catalog) is mandatory because the stale-leader TLA+ sabotage shows that re-deriving the incarnation after rebirth targets the new life directly, causing data loss.
In the current object model `ObjectKind` has only `Blob`; `Tree` and `CATR` were removed, while `PartManifest` is a protobuf body embedded in root-shard state.

Manifest debris must be drained before deleting the victim mount slot because deleting the mount body removes `floorForNamespace` watermark authority and would make the debris ineligible forever; the decommission command is the epoch authority and can sweep old-epoch prefixes.
B92 requires an adopted leaf to carry its real `blob_size` rather than a placeholder or zero value.
`system.blob_storage_log` does not log reads by default because `enable_blob_storage_log_for_read_operations` defaults to false and requires `enable_blob_storage_log`.

Scenario cards that check GC-reclaim progress mid-run (not just at the final checkpoint) must honor the condemn-grace period the same way the end-checkpoint does, or they miscount in-pipeline objects awaiting graduation as a leak; this miscalibration (not a product bug) caused a false-red S36 verdict and is a lesson for other scenario cards with mid-run reclaim assertions.

Blob safety requires a fresh in-body incarnation_tag for every upload, a backend token, and exact-token deletion; resurrecting a condemned blob re-uploads from the writer's source with a fresh tag.; The v3 cas_blob tag is a fresh random u128 per upload attempt and is the exact-token delete primitive; bld attributes newborn debris to the writer build
CI needed 6-hour-job-timeout sharding after a TSan lane finished 10,990/10,990 tests but was killed 16 seconds before it could report the result.

The revival invariant forbids reading a condemned or vanished blob to revive it; revival re-uploads the writer's own source bytes with a fresh incarnation. A condemned blob is never adopted or server-side-copied; it is recreated from the writer's own source bytes under a fresh `incarnation_tag`.
